components.css: .ds-label{min-height:44px;min-width:70px;padding:10px 7px 4px;background:transparent;border:0;color:#fff4d8;font:11px/1.2 'Segoe UI',sans-serif;text-shadow:0 1px 2px #101715,1px 0 3px #101715;white-space:nowrap;cursor:pointer}.ds-label>span:first-child{background:rgb(24 28 26 / 80%);padding:1px 4px}.ds-label[aria-pressed=true]{color:#ffe3a5}.ds-label[aria-pressed=true]>span:first-child{text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:3px}.ds-health{display:block;height:4px;max-width:72px;margin:4px auto 0;border:1px solid rgb(18 25 22 / 90%);background:#492f27}.ds-health>span{display:block;height:100%;background:#87bea4}.ds-action:focus-visible,.ds-utility:focus-visible,.ds-label:focus-visible,.ds-disclosure summary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #ffe0a3;outline-offset:3px;}

components.css: .ds-player{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;width:180px;padding:6px 8px 6px 4px;background:var(--panel,rgb(24 28 26 / 94%));border:1px solid var(--line,rgb(191 167 111 / 55%));color:#f5ecd8;font-family:'Segoe UI',system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-player>svg{width:40px;flex:0 0 40px;stroke:var(--gold,#edcd88);fill:#394440;stroke-width:1.4}.ds-player-info{flex:1;min-width:0}.ds-player-info strong{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:13px;font-weight:600}.ds-player-info strong span,.ds-player-info small{font-size:10px;font-weight:400;color:var(--muted,#d0c6af)}.ds-player-health{position:relative;height:15px;margin-top:4px;background:#361c17;border:1px solid #bc9172}.ds-player-health>span{display:block;height:100%;background:#a33d2e}.ds-player-health b{position:absolute;inset:0 4px;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;font-size:10px;font-weight:500;line-height:12px}

components.css: .ds-disclosure{background:var(--panel,rgb(24 28 26 / 94%));border:1px solid var(--line,rgb(191 167 111 / 55%));color:#f5ecd8;font-family:'Segoe UI',system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-disclosure summary{min-height:44px;padding:13px 14px;color:var(--gold,#edcd88);font-size:12px;cursor:pointer}.ds-disclosure[open] summary{border-bottom:1px solid var(--line,rgb(191 167 111 / 55%))}.ds-disclosure>div{max-height:27dvh;overflow-y:auto;padding:10px 12px;scrollbar-color:var(--bronze,#a58c59) #202522;scrollbar-width:thin}.ds-disclosure p{margin:10px 0 0;font-size:11px;line-height:1.5;color:var(--muted,#d0c6af)}.ds-action:focus-visible,.ds-utility:focus-visible,.ds-label:focus-visible,.ds-disclosure summary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #ffe0a3;outline-offset:3px;}

narrative.overview:
The classic fantasy HUD frames a playable 3D world with bronze hairlines, green-charcoal panels, and warm ivory lettering. Controls remain compact and familiar, with touch-sized actions and clear targeting feedback. The scene supplies the dimensional content; the interface supplies readable state.

Cormorant Garamond gives location names their fantasy character, while ordinary sans-serif labels keep actions and health understandable. The system uses original vector icons and procedural 3D content. It does not reproduce pixels, proprietary artwork, or simulated metal textures from the reference.
keyCharacteristics: Flat dark panels with bronze borders.
Warm serif location titles and practical sans-serif controls.
Touch-sized actions with compact supporting measurements.
Selection expressed by name emphasis, target details, and a ring in the world.

rules.name: The Readable Overlay Rule
rules.body: Text above the moving scene receives a stable dark backing or a soft text shadow; selection remains visible without relying on color alone.

rules.name: The Measured Type Rule
rules.body: Reserve monospace and tabular numerals for FPS, entity count, and coordinates.

rules.name: The Scene Depth Rule
rules.body: Let the rendered world provide depth. HUD panels remain flat, separated by thin borders rather than decorative bevels or large shadows.

dos: Do preserve the bronze, green-charcoal, and warm ivory relationship.
Do retain at least 44px-high interactive controls and visible keyboard focus.
Do pair icons with action labels and keep synthetic data identified.
Do keep entity names readable against changes in the 3D background.
donts: Don't copy proprietary game artwork or reference screenshot pixels.
Don't replace measured diagnostics with decorative charts or marketing statistics.
Don't use a serif display face for dense instructions or numeric diagnostics.
Don't add decorative material effects that compete with the rendered scene.
